novice.title: Novice Defender
novice.blurb: Threat modelling in five minutes a feature.

blocks.title: Four questions
blocks.body:
Threat modelling does not need a formal process to be worth doing. Four questions, asked out loud, catch most of it:

1. **What are we building?** A sketch, not a document.
2. **What can go wrong?** Who benefits from breaking this, and how?
3. **What are we going to do about it?** Per risk, one of: mitigate, accept, transfer, eliminate.
4. **Did we do a good job?** Revisit when the design changes.

The second question is the one teams skip, and it is the only one that finds anything.

blocks.title: This whole pack is the demo
blocks.body: Nothing in the application code knows this content exists. It was installed as a JSON file and a manifest entry.

questions.prompt: Which threat-modelling question do teams most often skip?

choices.text: Did we do a good job?

questions.explanation: It is the only question that actually surfaces new risk, and the easiest one to hand-wave.
